html.p: The Boxplot dataType (distinct from SimpleBoxplot) renders multiple grouped boxplot series side-by-side on the same x-axis. Use it when you need to compare distributions across two dimensions simultaneously — for example, machine vs. shift, or product line vs. day of week.

Unlike SimpleBoxplot, this builder consumes a transposed result table where each column is one boxplot and each row is one property. The table must have exactly 8 rows (plus optional outlier rows) and N columns (one per box):

td.b: Content of each cell (one cell per box)

tr.td: Category name — used as the series/legend label
X-axis group label — used as the xAxis tick label
Number of distinct categories (same value repeated in every cell)

html.p: The builder deduplicates row 5 to create the series list and row 6 to build the xAxis. Boxes with the same category name form one series; boxes with the same xAxis label are grouped together under that tick.
html.h1: Constructing the transposed table in Splunk
html.p: Because Splunk normally produces one-row-per-observation tables, you must build this transposed structure explicitly. The cleanest approach uses | append to stack exactly 8 result rows and | sort seq to guarantee row order.

The factory example below compares component thickness (mm) measured on two CNC machines across two production shifts (Morning and Afternoon). There are 4 boxes in total: CNC-01 Morning, CNC-01 Afternoon, CNC-02 Morning, CNC-02 Afternoon.

pre.code: | makeresults count=1 | eval seq=1, c0="5.72", c1="5.68", c2="5.78", c3="5.75" | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=2, c0="5.76", c1="5.73", c2="5.82", c3="5.79"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=3, c0="5.79", c1="5.76", c2="5.85", c3="5.83"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=4, c0="5.83", c1="5.80", c2="5.89", c3="5.87"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=5, c0="5.89", c1="5.86", c2="5.96", c3="5.93"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=6, c0="Morning", c1="Afternoon", c2="Morning", c3="Afternoon"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=7, c0="CNC-01", c1="CNC-01", c2="CNC-02", c3="CNC-02"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=8, c0="2", c1="2", c2="2", c3="2"] | sort seq | table c0 c1 c2 c3

html.p: The | sort seq is essential — it guarantees that min is always row 0 and the category count is always row 7, regardless of how Splunk internally orders same-time makeresults events. The final | table c0 c1 c2 c3 drops the seq and internal _time fields, leaving only the 4 data columns.
Mapping the columns to the expected layout:

The builder will extract two series: Afternoon and Morning (alphabetically sorted after deduplication of row 5). Each series will have two data points corresponding to CNC-01 and CNC-02 (alphabetically sorted from row 6).

search.query: | makeresults count=1 | eval seq=1, c0="5.72", c1="5.68", c2="5.78", c3="5.75" | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=2, c0="5.76", c1="5.73", c2="5.82", c3="5.79"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=3, c0="5.79", c1="5.76", c2="5.85", c3="5.83"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=4, c0="5.83", c1="5.80", c2="5.89", c3="5.87"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=5, c0="5.89", c1="5.86", c2="5.96", c3="5.93"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=6, c0="Morning", c1="Afternoon", c2="Morning", c3="Afternoon"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=7, c0="CNC-01", c1="CNC-01", c2="CNC-02", c3="CNC-02"] | append [| makeresults count=1 | eval seq=8, c0="2", c1="2", c2="2", c3="2"] | sort seq | table c0 c1 c2 c3

html.h1: Extending to more machines and shifts
html.p: To add a third machine (CNC-03), add one column per shift (c4 and c5) to every row, update the category row to include Morning and Afternoon for the new columns, update the xAxis row to CNC-03, and change the nCategories row to keep the value at 2 (still 2 shift categories).
To add a third shift category, add new columns and update the nCategories value in row 7 to 3. The builder automatically creates an additional series for the new category name.
Important: the nCategories value controls how the builder partitions the columns into groups. It must equal the number of unique values in row 5. If they do not match, the grouping will be incorrect.
html.h1: When to choose SimpleBoxplot vs Boxplot

tr.td: One boxplot per row, single series, optional outliers
Multiple grouped series on one x-axis (e.g. machine x shift)
SPL query produces statistics with | stats perc25 ... BY group
Comparing shifts / time windows side-by-side for multiple assets
